Alexandru Macedonski (14 March 1854 – 24 November 1920) was a Romanian poet, novelist, dramatist, and literary critic who promoted French Symbolism in Romania and led the Romanian Symbolist movement. He was a pioneering figure in local modernist literature, credited as the first Romanian author to use free verse and possibly the first in modern European literature. Often compared to Mihai Eminescu, Macedonski led a cosmopolitan trend through his "Literatorul" journal, opposing Eminescu's traditionalism.

Initially a Neoromantic, Macedonski transitioned through Realist-Naturalist and Symbolist stages, advocating for "instrumentalism" while maintaining ties to Neoclassicism. His major works include the "Nights" cycle and collections like "Prima verba" and "Excelsior." A civil servant and journalist, Macedonski's fluctuating political allegiance led to numerous controversies, notably with the "Junimea" society and during World War I. He was also involved in esotericism and inventing. Macedonski came from a notable political family, being the son of General Alexandru Macedonski and the grandson of 1821 rebel Dimitrie Macedonski.

PCOF ta- bles exist within casualty categories of wounded in action,  nonbattle injuries, disease and outpatient visits for a given  combat or noncombat scenario throughout the range of  military operations (ROMO). ROMO is defined for this effort  to include humanitarian assistance, disaster relief, defense  support of civil authorities and various combat operations.  The military medical planning community, until now, lacked  a functional and accurate means of estimating PCOFs,  which are necessary to develop the patient streams used  in health care simulations.

The McDonnell Douglas MD-11 is an American tri-jet wide-body airliner, initially manufactured by McDonnell Douglas and later by Boeing. Launched on December 30, 1986, the first prototype was assembled beginning March 9, 1988. Its maiden flight occurred on January 10, 1990, with FAA certification following on November 8. The first delivery to Finnair was on December 7, and it entered service on December 20, 1990.

The MD-11 retained the basic trijet design of the DC-10 but featured updated engines, a slightly larger wingspan with winglets, and an increased maximum takeoff weight. It has a stretched fuselage to accommodate 298 passengers and a glass cockpit that eliminates the need for a flight engineer. However, the MD-11 failed to meet range and fuel efficiency targets, resulting in poor sales with only 200 units built, many of which were converted to freighters after passenger use declined. The last MD-11 was built in October 2000.
